The library smells of old paper and dust - like knowledge, like expectations.

All of which Phainon isn’t living up to in his current state of affairs. It’s woven into the worn leather spines and the yellowed pages of books that have passed through countless hands, and now into his. There’s something quietly reverent about it, something heavy, as though the weight of every unread word presses against the silence. The scent lingers in the air, tickling his nose as he withholds another sneeze from the particles floating around.

Phainon never spends much time here. Not because he doesn’t appreciate knowledge - he does, or he wouldn’t be bothering to pursue an engineering degree - but because he prefers learning by doing rather than reading.

Words on a page feel static, unmoving, detached from reality, whereas when things move, they are tangible enough to touch and build, and that’s when he thrives. But here, in the vast stillness of the library, where he’s afraid to breathe too loudly, everything exists in a world of paper or laptop screens.

It’s far too quiet. Phainon isn’t used to not having constant background noise, whether that’s in the form of a low hum of life happening around him, friends chatting, coffee machines whirring, or even music playing through his headphones. Here, the only sounds are the occasional rustling of pages, the quiet click click of keyboards, the distant scratch of a pen and the rhythmic tick of the grand old clock mounted on the wall above him. It’s the kind of silence that demands something of you, that makes you hyper-aware of every inhale, every shift in your seat, every absent-minded tap of your fingers against the desk.

The dim glow of antique desk lamps casts long shadows across the rows of bookshelves, stretching between towering aisles like pathways to another world. It makes the library seem gloomier than it actually is, considering it’s daylight outside. Phainon feels like he’s stuck in a relic of another era -

heavy oak tables, worn-out chairs, the faint creak of floorboards beneath careful steps. It’s the kind of place that whispers rather than speaks, that judges you for being too loud, too restless, too alive.

Phainon exhales, slumping over the open book in front of him, no longer caring if he disturbs the stillness. He hates this - despises it, in fact - but if he wants to pass this module, he’s going to have to focus. Yet when he tries to do just that, the words on the page begin blurring together, diagrams no longer making any sense as he stares at them. He could use his laptop, but the thing barely works on a good day, let alone using the public wifi available. His assignments are due at midnight tomorrow, which leaves him plenty of time, but not when he’s spending most of it ruminating on how much he’d rather be anywhere else. All his friends are busy doing their own things, such as living their lives, free of assignments because they don’t put them off until the last minute like he does. It’s his fault, but it doesn’t make the knowledge any easier to swallow.

Frowning, he sits up again, glaring down at the book like that’ll fix everything. He shoves his hand underneath the front cover, flipping it shut in a childish outburst of spite.

“Please don’t slam the books.” A stern voice cuts through the stillness.

Phainon jumps in fright, clutching at his chest to will his heartbeat to slow as he turns to face the person who interrupted his brooding. As soon as he takes in what’s before him, he forgets how to think.

A man stands across from him, arms folded neatly across his chest, watching him behind a pair of simple black frames that suggest he’s already written Phainon off as a lost cause. He’s sharp and poised, biceps bulging even beneath his loose-fitting jumper, and the worn edges of the neckline leave a sliver of his clavicle on display that Phainon can’t seem to look away from. There’s something tattooed on his skin, swirling and red, that captures his attention more than the textbook in front of him ever did. It contrasts with the muted colour of his jumper, which looks so soft it could be wool or even cashmere.

Distantly, Phainon notices the lanyard looped around his neck, an ID card hanging from the end of it. The plastic catches the glow of the desk lamp, reflecting a faint gleam as it sways, practically begging him to take a look.

Without thinking, Phainon leans forward, his curiosity outweighing his better judgement. The tiny, pixelated photo on the card shows the same sharp gestures now illuminated before him - blonde hair tousled just enough to suggest some form of styling goes into it, amber eyes caught in an impersonal, official stare. Even in a low-resolution ID photo, he looks striking.

There’s a block of text beside the image, too small to make out in the dim light, but two words stand out, bold and capitalised, demanding attention: HEAD LIBRARIAN. Phainon expected something else, maybe a security guard going by the guy’s well-defined build and height. The title feels no less weighty, as though he’s just met the king of the castle. This guy isn’t just anyone, clearly. Phainon jolts, realising too late that he’s been obvious with his staring. The moment stretches, thick with words unspoken before he forces himself to look away, suddenly hyper-aware of the stillness between them. He swallows, his throat dry as if the air itself has changed -

charged with something he can’t quite understand. His cheeks flush as he laughs nervously, trying to break up the awkwardness that he created. It doesn’t help that he feels severely underdressed, suddenly conscious of how terrible he probably looks in comparison: running on nothing but coffee and a quick nap, dressed in a bright yellow t-shirt paired with a pair of purple shorts.

He should really say something. Apologise, probably, and make a joke that he didn’t realise that he’d slammed the book closed at all. Maybe, he could even ask for help to see if there are any other materials the library holds that could aid him. Unfortunately, he does none of that, his brain short-circuiting instead, struck dumb by the realisation that he finds this stranger - this disapproving, clearly no-nonsense librarian - unreasonably attractive.

“Right, yeah. Sorry.” Phainon finally stutters out, clearing his throat and trying to shake off the ridiculous thoughts going around his head.

The librarian doesn’t respond, electing to only give him a slow, assessing blink before turning away, and walking back to where Phainon presumes the front desk is. Just like that, he’s been dismissed, probably never to be

taken seriously ever again. Phainon sighs, dragging a hand through his hair, cringing at how oily his roots feel.

Maybe it’s time to just go home.

Phainon has no intention of going back to the library the next day. He assures himself it’s because the place is suffocating - too quiet, too serious, too full of books he’ll never understand - but deep down, he knows it’s because of him. The librarian. The one with the sharp gaze and the unreadable expression. The one who barely looked at him and yet somehow managed to make him feel like a complete idiot with a single sentence.

It was stupid, really. Hardly the most humiliating thing he’s ever done -

especially considering he’s still best friends with Castorice, who has witnessed nearly every mortifying moment in his life since they were kids.

She was there when he tripped on stage during a school assembly in Year 9, sprawled flat on his face in front of the entire school population. She was there when he spent three whole weeks convinced his physics teacher had a personal vendetta against him, only to realise that she hadn’t been glaring at him at all, but instead squinting due to her bad eyesight. She was even there when he’d had his first kiss with a girl in his class behind the bike shed, sitting with Castorice afterwards on the floor of his bedroom, eating crisps straight from the packet while he swore up and down it wasn’t that good, honestly. And yet, despite a history filled with moments that should have been far more embarrassing, this one clings to him the most. It’s not as though the librarian was cruel or dismissive, he hadn’t even stuck around long enough for that, yet still, the encounter leaves a lingering heat in his chest whenever he thinks about it. Which, considering how little time has passed since it happened, has been a lot.

Castorice would tell him he’s overreacting. She’d roll her eyes, shove a biscuit dipped into tea into his mouth, and tell him to get over himself.

Normally, she’s the first person he tells everything - every triumph, every disaster, every stupid, fleeting moment in between despite the physical distance between them due to attending different universities. She’s the one who gets the first text at an ungodly hour after he gets into an argument with his parents ( i’m coming over, unlock ur door pls), to the moment he called her when he got his acceptance letter for engineering at his dream university. She knows him - the unpolished, unfiltered, messy version of him that no one else gets to see. And yet, despite all that and more, he can’t bring himself to bring up their text conversation and type a simple so i met a guy.’ All that’d do would open a can of worms he hasn’t even begun to do himself, to delve deeper into the stranger in the library with the cool, unreadable gaze, the one who made his stomach twist in a way he’s never felt before.

It should be easy to mention - just another one of his passing stories that they exchange daily in their text conversations, another stupid thing to laugh about over coffee, perhaps, but every time he thinks about saying it, the words never make it into reality. Phainon guesses it could also be because there’s not much to tell. Like, oh, the librarian on campus probably hates me bc i slammed closed one of his precious books, lol. But none of that encompasses all the other unnecessary feelings he’s been saddled with alongside it.

So, for his own sake, and possibly for his sanity, too, he stays away.

He finds other places to study instead, bouncing from one spot to the other in a futile attempt to settle. Even his dorm room isn’t quite right, leading to another bout of restlessness that makes him feel jittery all over. He chooses

to go to the café near campus first. He thought he was used to noise, usually revelling in the sounds of clattering of cups and the constant murmur of conversation, but now it makes him feel uneasy. The next spot he goes to, lugging his textbooks and laptop bag strung over one shoulder, is the student lounge. Somehow, it’s even worse. He knew there was a reason he’d stopped frequenting it a week after he started uni - and it seems that reason hasn’t changed: there’s always someone playing terrible dubstep music from a half-broken speaker at any given time. To get any work done here would require an unreal amount of concentration and dedication, both of which he’s currently lacking. His last choice is the common room, which should’ve been a reasonable alternative, but proves useless when he finds himself too easily pulled into side conversations with his fellow students, too eager for distractions that let him ignore the growing anxiety clawing at his chest.

None of these places are good for concentration, and he’s not entirely sure how he managed before studying there during the past 2 years. Defeated, he makes his way back to his dorm room, grumpy and overstimulated from a wasted day.

As Phainon clicks Submit on his second to last assignment - the clock turning from 7:59 pm to 8:00 pm, he catches himself thinking about the library again. Or, more specifically, the person in the library. There’s a small amount of relief at almost being done for the week in catching up with his work, but it’s overtaken by more aimless thoughts. Phainon wonders if he’d even recognise him if he went back, or if he’s already erased him from his memory, just another nameless student making noise when they shouldn’t. He should be grateful he didn’t care. He should be relieved that he probably hasn't spared him a second thought. Instead, the idea of being forgotten gnaws at him in a way he can’t explain.

Frustration bubbles over as he stares blankly at his laptop screen, the words You have successfully submitted your assignment blurring together as though it’s a mass equation he can’t get his head around. He needs to focus, needs to study, needs to stop spiralling over some librarian who he’s only met once. The longer he sits there, the extent of what he needs to do weighing on his shoulders, the 0% Completed next to his last assignment feeling like a hole in his head, the more obvious it becomes. He can’t keep pretending to avoid the library as though it’s helping him. He isn’t getting anything done. And as much as he wants to deny it, the truth is inescapable: right now, the library is the best place to finish his work. Phainon just has to suck it up and go back. He’s a big boy, fully grown and well into adulthood, surely he can brave it one more time? Maybe it’ll scratch this itch once and for all, and then he can go about living his life as he’d done before.

It’s fine, anyway - it’s not like he has to interact with the librarian. Easy: he’ll keep his head down, find a quiet corner far, far away from the front desk, and actually get his work done. That’s all. No ridiculous overthinking, no pointless distractions, and thank the gods, no dubstep music to be heard.

With that in mind, and with a quick glance at the clock - it’s now 8:30 pm, which means he’ll have a few hours to finish this final assignment before the deadline ends - he shoves his laptop into his bag and collects his textbooks, pulling on a varsity jacket as he heads out across campus before he can talk himself out of it.

It only takes a few minutes to get from his dorm to the library, but tonight, the walk feels different. The crisp evening air is a relief after spending hours holed up in his room, where the walls seemed to press in, thick with the stale scent of unfinished coffee and the weight of unproductive studying. Out here, the cool breeze sharpens his senses, brushing against his

warm skin, coaxing him to wake up and giving him enough energy to continue for the rest of the night. Phainon isn’t against pulling all-nighters, but considering how late he’d left his assignments, he doesn’t have that choice: once the clock hits midnight, it’s all over for him.

He inhales deeply, the air clean with the distant scent of damp earth and fallen leaves. Autumn time is one of his favourites, the campus turning into a rich mix of yellow and orange hues, the trees turning bare ready for the winter months. The pathways are busy despite the late hour, clusters of students weaving past him, some laughing and some lost in their own worlds, faces illuminated by the glow of their phone screens. The faint hum of conversations and rhythmic tapping of his shoes against concrete creates a familiar soundtrack to campus life at night: active, yet subdued, a transition between the chaos of the day and the quiet evening.

Phainon walks quickly, hands shoved in his jacket pockets, his breath coming out in soft clouds in the chill. He tells himself he’s in a rush because he needs to study, needs to make the most of this new-found awakeness, the final hours before the deadline ticking down at an alarming rate. The library will welcome him as it always has - with its dim golden lighting and the scent of polished wood, allowing him to work in peace. Shaking the thought of the blonde man away before it can begin, he quickens his pace, his trainers scuffing against the pavement. The sooner he gets there, the sooner he can get this over and done with.

The moment he steps through the heavy oak doors of the library, the now familiar scent of old paper and dust once again washes over him, grounding and suffocating all at once. The air inside is a lot thicker than the brisk breeze outside, the contrast sending goosebumps across his arms as he

shivers. He bolsters himself, straightening his spine and holding his head high. He has a right to be here! This is his university campus, and the only library on site, of which he’s perfectly entitled to use regardless of anything else. Albeit he hadn’t made much use of it in the past, but he can turn over a new leaf, can’t he? He can find the appeal in the quietness, the silent comradery of the other students focusing on their tasks too, headphones on and locked in.

Phainon’s confidence holds for approximately five seconds - right up until his gaze drifts towards the front desk and lands on him. He’s sitting back in an office chair, legs spread wide, flipping through a thick hardcover. The glow of the desk lamp casts long shadows across the multitude of angles of his face, highlighting the lines of his cheekbones, the elegant slope of his nose, and the precise cut of his jaw. It turns each feature into something almost sculptural, like what he’d seen at the local history museum in the marble sculptures from the Greek period. His glasses have slid slightly down the bridge of his nose, and when he pushes them up absentmindedly with his forefinger, Phainon’s eyes follow the motion without thinking.

There’s something effortlessly composed about him, an air of solitude and coolness, striking in the way his expression remains neutral and focused, as if nothing in the world could shake him. It only makes his beauty more infuriating, and almost affirms the stirring emotions it’d caused Phainon yesterday. It isn’t the kind that demands attention, loud and obvious - it’s the kind that sneaks up on you, refined and deliberate, like the pages of a rare book worn smooth at the edges but still pristine beneath careful hands.

He should step away, go and find that desk in the corner of the room, far away from the front desk just like he’d promised himself. But for a brief, stupid moment, he forgets why he’s there. His mind blanks, caught on the curve of the librarian’s downturned lips, the way the light grazes the side of his throat and dips into the hollows of his exposed collarbones, those

curious red tattoos peeking through the top few buttons of an undone shirt.

The guy is unfairly pretty in a rugged type of way, where the handsomeness of his face and built body should take precedence over anything else and yet can’t compare to the delicate way his eyelashes flutter against the highs of his cheekbones.

A beat passes, and Phainon’s chest tightens, the feeling unfamiliar and unwelcome. He swallows hard, and he should keep his mouth shut, but he’s walking up to the front desk before he can stop himself. His pulse ticks unreasonably fast, and he tells himself it’s just because he’s sleep-deprived and only running on the latte and croissant he had early this morning during his brief stint at the cafe, and not because the librarian still hasn’t noticed him, completely absorbed in whatever he’s reading.

He clears his throat, dumping his bag onto the front desk with a clack, his laptop hitting the wood.

Big mistake.

The librarian glances up, eyes narrowed in clear annoyance at the disturbance, and now Phainon actually has to speak. Shit, he hadn’t planned this far ahead.

“Uh, hey,” His voice comes out slightly hoarse, so he clears his throat again, and then immediately regrets it when the librarian arches a single, perfectly unimpressed brow at his entrance.

“...Can I help you?” He asks, tone as measured and calm as the day before.

Phainon nods, his head lolling up and down like a muppet. He realises he’s going to have to answer that with more than a gesture. “Yeah, I just - um, I need to return this.” He lifts the textbook in his hands as proof, gripping it far too tightly. He doesn’t need to return it at all, it’s his damn book, one that he had to pay out of his yearly tuition allowance. This is the most stupid, ridiculous, embarrassing thing he’s ever done, and yet: “Since, you know, that’s… what libraries are for.”

The librarian blinks at him, his head tilting ever so slightly, the braid in his hair swinging gently from the movement. “That is what libraries are for, yes.”

Phainon wants to die. Right here, right now, between the bookshelves, crushed beneath the weight of his incompetence to act like a normal human being. But no, he keeps going, because apparently, he’s incapable of cutting his losses. In for a penny, in for a pound, right? He robotically dumps the book onto the counter, waiting with bated breath as the librarian slowly puts down the hardback in favour of Phainon’s. The guy looks up at him sceptically before picking it up, flipping it open to check the borrowing slip.

Only, with the dawning realisation on both of their faces, there isn’t one.

Instead, there’s a slightly crumpled-up receipt from a secondhand bookshop tucked inside the dust jacket.

The librarian’s gaze lifts back to him, completely unreadable. “This isn’t a library book.”

Phainon frowns, his brain scrambling to process the words. “What?”

The librarian sighs sharply, as though inconvenience beyond belief, which Phainon supposes he technically is, and turns the book around, tapping the inside cover with his knuckle. “There’s no stamp. No borrowing record.

This is your book.”

Phainon stares. Then, because he’s stupid and his brain is still unable to comprehend anything, he blurts out: “No, it’s not.”

A pause. The librarian looks pointedly at the receipt. Phainon’s receipt, with his name and tutor group number scrawled across the top.

“Oh,” He says, voice hollow, “Oh, my god.”

Heat floods his face as the full weight of his stupidity crashes down on him like a bucket of ice water. He tries to think of a way to salvage this, but there is no way. He’s doomed. He has just marched up to the hot librarian and tried to return a book that he personally owns, one that he knew he owned. He wishes the dark brown flooring would open up and swallow him whole.

The librarian, to his credit, doesn’t laugh. His expression hardly changes, but there’s something suspiciously close to amusement lighting his eyes.

“Did you mean to return another book?”

Phainon shakes his head, dazed. “No. I - I think I just -” He gestures vaguely at the air as if that explains anything. “I wasn’t… paying attention.”

“Clearly.” The librarian snaps the book shut with a sense of finality and hands it back, their fingers brushing together for the briefest moment. The touch is cool, steady - completely unfazed - unlike Phainon, who feels he might combust into smithereens.

He takes the book back too quickly, practically snatching it away and nearly dropping it in the process. He grips it like it’s suddenly a live grenade, and it might as well be considering he’d just about blown up any confidence he had left in this exchange. Phainon needs to leave, like, immediately, but he also needs to study and finish his assignment.

“Okay, well, I’ll just - um - go.”

The librarian inclines his head in a quiet farewell, not even deigning Phainon with a vocal response, and without a word, returns back to the book he’d been reading before this disaster occurred as if it never happened.

Phainon turns on his heels, the soles of his trainers squeaking horrendously loud against the polished floor, and speed-walks toward the corner of the room. Just as he’s about to be out of earshot, he catches the faintest sound from behind him. A breath - not quite a laugh, more of a scoff than anything else, but a noise close to humour either way.

And somehow, that’s the most humiliating part of it all.

Phainon sinks into a chair in one of the more secluded areas, chucking the damning textbook and his bag onto the table with more force than necessary. A few loose sheets flutter dangerously close to the edge of falling off, and he has to snatch them up before they slip to the floor. Focus, he tells himself as he settles, taking his bulky laptop out of his bag and setting it on the table. He opens it, the welcome screen already waiting for him as he types in his password. His browser is still up, endless amounts of tabs loading in as the internet automatically connects to the library wifi.

While it does that, he flips open his textbook, eyes skimming over dense paragraphs of text without absorbing a single word. He forces himself to slow down, taking a deep breath as he focuses back on the top of the page, but it’s like his brain is coated in static. Nothing sticks. The numbers and theories blur together, meaningless.

Sharp cheekbones.

Phainon shakes his head, trying to reset. Hand hovering over his touchpad and the other rubbing the pages of his textbook together to soothe himself, he tries again. The words keep slipping through his brain like a sieve, and his mind keeps drifting back.

Amber eyes.

His grip turns punishing, almost ripping the paper, and his hand clatters against the keyboard, leaving a random group of letters in the search bar.

Before he can clear it, his phone pings with a notification. Phainon fishes it

out of his jacket pocket, waiting for his Face ID to unlock it for him as it opens up directly into his text messages.

His fingers tighten together, knuckles pressing against one another as he cracks them in quick succession - a small ritual, a desperate attempt of centering himself.

Three hours. Well, not even that as his laptop clock says it’s now 9:30 pm.

That’s all he has left, 2 and a half measly hours to pull together something passable, to stitch his half-baked ideas into words that resemble a coherent

thought and a passing grade. He glances down at his notebook strewn next to his laptop - his writing is hurried, scattered and chaotic, full of frantic underlines and doodles. It’s an absolute mess.

He sighs again, planting his elbows on the table, fingers poised over the keyboard with a renewed determination. The clock is against him, and he’s still coming down from the most embarrassing moment of his life, but he’ll get this done and with time to spare, he bets.

Phainon isn’t sure what happens after he presses Submit on his final assessment, only that relief floods his system so heavily that it feels like he’s going to pass out. The next thing he knows, a voice is dragging him back to consciousness - steady, quiet, with just the faintest trace of exasperation.

“You shouldn’t sleep here.”

Phainon stirs, groggy and disoriented. His face is pressed against the open pages of his textbook, the words smudged from where his breath has warmed the paper. His limbs feel sluggish as he pushes himself upright, blinking against the desk lamp that feels all too bright now. It takes a second for his mind to catch up, to register the figure standing beside him.

Sharp features, warm amber eyes, posture straight and composed even in the late hours of the night.

The librarian.

Oh, no.

Embarrassment strikes like a slap to the face. He barely remembers falling asleep, only that he cheered quietly to himself when he saw the 100%

completed next to his assignment, before flopping forward in exhaustion.

Now that he’s awake the weight of it - of this - settles over him like a thick blanket of shame. He’s not even sure what’s worse: the fact that he passed out in the middle of the library, or that he was the one to find him.

“I -” His voice cracks, hoarse from sleep. He clears his throat quickly, blinking rapidly and sitting up straighter. “I wasn’t -” Phainon stops, realising mid-sentence that there’s no point in denying it. He has no idea what time it is or how long he was out for, only that he’s been caught red-handed. The evidence is probably all over his face, smudged ink and drool crusting at the edge of his lips. He groans softly, rubbing at his temple.

“Sorry about that.”

The librarian - Phainon should really figure out his name, he’s sick of not having one to put to his face at this point - of course, doesn’t let him off easy by just leaving it there. He just tilts his head, gaze steady: “The library closes in ten minutes.” He says, voice flat like they’re not witnessing Phainon scrub at his lips to get rid of drool that’d leaked out during his nap.

“You should start packing up.”

Phainon chuckles humourlessly, dragging a hand through his tousled hair.

“Yeah, will do.” He closes his laptop, flipping his textbook and notebook shut as he stacks everything in a pile ready to be put back into his bag.

Silence stretches between them for a moment, save for a distant creak of a floorboard somewhere deeper in the library. Phainon wonders if it’s just them now, the only two left inside. The air feels heavier than it should with that thought. The librarian hasn’t walked away yet, and his gaze is starting to make Phainon nervous, fidgeting in his seat as he shoves everything in his bag without any finesse. The zip jams as he tries to close it, getting caught on the spiral of his notebook sticking out. With a grumble, he pushes everything in as far as it can go.

“Falling asleep over your books isn’t exactly effective studying.”

Phainon jerks, head spinning to look up at the blonde man. He lets out a tired laugh, half genuine and half self-deprecating. “Yeah, well, straight A student here. So something must be working.”

For the first time, an emotion flickers in his expression. It’s small, barely there - a faint twitch at the corner of his lips, a ghost of a smirk. Not quite amused, his eyes still boring into Phainon without a trace of a spark, but close.

“Really?”

“Really,” Phainon emphasises, standing up and slinging his bag over his shoulder. He realises this is closer than they’ve ever been, and he blinks at the subtle height difference. He assumed the other was slightly taller, what with his bulkier build and the way he carried himself, but it turns out there’s a few inches difference in them. It’s not much - their eyes still meet without any trouble - but the thought sends butterflies tumbling through his stomach.

The librarian hums, cocking their head to the left as he takes Phainon in.

His gaze moves slowly - deliberate, assessing. Phainon feels the weight of it as it drags over his face, pausing just long enough that his breath catches before it dips lower. Over the rumpled fabric of his t-shirt, across the way he haphazardly tucked it into the waistband of his jeans, the rips across his knees and thighs. His eyes flicker down even lower, down to his scuffed trainers, then just as unhurriedly, his gaze traces its way back up - lingering this time, as though piecing Phainon together from the inside out, as though trying to put together a puzzle.

Phainon shifts his weight onto his right leg. Is he a mess? Is he about to get kicked out, an official public nuisance for sleeping in the library? Finally, amber eyes meet his again, as unreadable as ever.

“Perhaps you’d be an A- plus student if you studied while awake.”

Phainon groans, shoulders slumping, whatever tension between them breaking. “Hey, don’t be mean! And that doesn’t exist, thankfully.”

The librarian raises an eyebrow, the faintest hint of amusement shaping his features. “Doesn’t exist?” He echoes, voice smooth, teasing. “Are you sure about that?”

Phainon crosses his arms, huffing dramatically. “Pretty sure if there was a higher grade, someone would’ve told me by now.”

A hum, “Or maybe no one bothered because they assumed you wouldn’t be aiming for it.”

Phainon gapes at him, affronted. What minor victory he had held at making the guy amused is sharply turning into wanting to rival this guy’s words.

Phainon has already suffered enough around him at his own expense.

“Wow, wow. First you wake me up, then you insult my academic ambition?

Harsh, much?”

The librarian scoffs, “If you had any real ambition, you wouldn’t have fallen asleep in the first place.”

Phainon scowls, but there’s no real bite to it. “Listen here, um -” He pauses, realising that he still doesn’t have a name. He peers down at the lanyard, enough so that he can finally make out a name. Mydeimos Kremnos.

The name tumbles from his lips all too easily. “Mydeimos -”

Mydeimos’s face curls up in disgust, eyes crinkling behind his glasses. “Just Mydei.”

“Okay, sure, cool, just Mydei,” Phainon says, trying not to laugh as Mydei’s expression sours even further. “Aren’t you supposed to encourage the students here or something?”

“Not part of my job,” Mydei replies tautly, “I’m here to keep students like you in check. Which -” Mydei brings up his arm, making a show of looking at his wristwatch. “You have 1 minute to leave before I lock you in here.”

“You wouldn’t!” Phainon gasps, genuinely startled by the fact that it’s almost midnight already. He must’ve slept for well over an hour then.

Mydei sneers, tilting his head down to look at Phainon over the rim of his glasses. “Don’t push me.”

“Fine, fine,” Phainon relents, walking past Mydei, making sure their shoulders brush against each other.

Mydei smells faintly of something sweet - subtle but distinct, lingering in the air between them. It’s not overpowering, nor artificial like some of the sickly perfumes people drown themselves in. No, this is softer, more natural, like a ripe fruit warmed by the sun. There’s a hint of tartness

beneath it, crisp and fresh, but the sweetness is what lingers the longest, curling about Phainon’s senses like a hook he can’t shake loose.

He wants to know what it is - whether it’s cologne, or if it’s Mydei’s shampoo, or if it’s just him. Phainon wants to lean in closer, to breathe deeper, to chase the scent until he can name it. But that would be insane.

And obvious. And most definitely weird.

Still, it clings to him even after Mydei shifts away, the ghost of it teasing his senses as he exhales. As he wanders back through the shelves to the exit, Phainon swears it follows him, clinging to his jacket like it’s haunting him in the best way possible.

Sunlight spills through the thin curtains, golden and insistent, creeping across the room until it lands directly on Phainon’s face. He groans, shifting onto his side, dragging his duvet higher as if that will somehow shield him from the morning’s intrusion. It doesn’t. The warmth finds him anyway, seeping into his skin, and lighting up the backs of his eyelids in a soft, hazy glow.

He buries his face deeper into the pillow, sighing as the heat lulls him somewhere between wakefulness and sleep. For a brief moment, he lets himself sink into it - the quiet hum of the world outside his window, the faint rustle of leaves in the breeze, the way the sun kisses his cheeks, gentle and calming. It’s nice. It’s peaceful, and it almost makes him want to stay like this all day. He hasn’t had the chance to wake up like this in who knows how long, his alarm ringing at stupid o’clock in the morning so he

can prepare for his morning lectures. Despite none of that, his body betrays him, a slow blink dragging him further into consciousness. His silver lashes stick together, his eyes dry and crusty with sleep. Phainon squints, groaning as he rubs at them half-heartedly.

It takes a second for reality to catch up to him, but when it does, the relief is instant. It’s Saturday. No deadlines looming over his head anymore, no reason to race across campus in hopes of finding a place to study, and no early lectures to drag himself out of bed for. Just a whole day stretched out before him, open and unclaimed. A rare moment of freedom.

And yet, despite the absolute lack of obligations given to him in this current moment, he still feels a little restless. Phainon stares up at the ceiling, blinking sluggishly as the final remnants of sleep slip away. His body feels heavy, still tired, weighed down by the warmth of his duvet, yet his mind is already stirring, thoughts drifting aimlessly. He could stay in bed for a little longer - hell, he should stay in bed considering how early it is - but the energy coiling in his limbs won’t let him.

With a deep sigh, he pushes himself upright, the sheets pooling around his waist as he runs a hand through his hair. It’s a mess, sticking up in every direction, and when he catches his reflection in the mirror across the room, he grimaces. Not his best look, that’s for sure. His eyelids are swollen, cheeks puffy and skin more pallid than usual with help from the dark circles under his eyes. The dorm room is quiet, the usual chaos of his comings and goings momentarily stilled.

Phainon grabs his phone from the nightstand, the screen lighting up the moment his fingers wrap around it. The glow of the screen feels too bright after just waking up, and he squints at it, blinking away the last blur of sleep

still clinging to his vision. The battery icon in the corner is fully charged, the cable loosely hanging from the bottom as he tugs it free and tosses it aside.

A cluster of notifications fills the screen - some from uni group chats, a few from his email, and one from an app reminding him about an assignment that, thankfully, he already submitted last night before passing out. At that, he cringes, shuddering before he can dwell on the memory of what occurred last night. He scrolls past it all, barely paying attention when a stack of messages from Castorice catches his eye. She’d sent it late last night after he’d already fallen asleep back in his dorm room. A quick tap opens their conversation, and he sees the string of texts: first, a gif of a cat aggressively typing, and then a dramatic ‘ you better be working on that paper and not ogling the hot librarian’ followed by an all-caps message 45 minutes later:

‘ PHAINON??? ’

Phainon huffs out a small laugh, shaking his head fondly as he types out a belated reply.

sorry i was asleep, but i did finish my assignment no ogling occurred

With his strong biceps flexing underneath the thin shirt as he moved, the cute braid in his hair, and his long legs wrapped in tight trousers. Anyway, he doesn’t expect Castorice to reply this early considering it’s the weekend, so he goes back to filtering

Unfortunately, he moves so fast that his chair begins to tip, his sense of gravity thrown off. His mouth opens to yell, stomach swooping when a hand comes slamming down on the back of the chair, immediately righting it again. Phainon’s chest heaves, heart racing, as he takes in Mydei in front of him.

One hand is holding onto a bottle of water, the other stretched out behind him, holding Phainon’s chair steady. Mydei’s shirt sleeves are rolled up to his elbows, showing off the way his muscles flex with power and strength.

Protruding lines of veins wrap underneath his skin like vines, which is something Phainon never thought he’d find attractive until now. He’s caught between wanting to stare more at his arms and looking at Mydei’s face and belatedly chooses the face option, which is staring down at him with a concerned scowl plastered across it. There are faint lines between his eyebrows, making Phainon want to smooth them out with his finger.

“You’re fast,” Phainon remarks, his heart still beating in his throat, now not just because of almost falling over but because of the man in front of him.

“And strong.”

Mydei doesn’t bother replying to that, which Phainon is secretly glad about.

Instead, he removes his hand from the back of Phainon’s chair and stands up straight, shoving the water bottle into Phainon’s face.

“Here.”

Phainon blinks owlishly at it before he slowly reaches up and grabs the bottle, the ice-cold temperature shocking him awake even more than the fright of almost falling over did. “I thought drinks weren’t allowed in the library?”

“Only if they don’t have a twist cap, which this one does,” Mydei gestures to it, encouraging Phainon to take a sip.

He does. The cool water slides down his dry throat like an oasis, and he downs half the bottle before he can stop himself.

Phainon gasps, licking a stray droplet away from his lips. He looks up at Mydei to find him already looking, staring intently at his mouth. “Thanks.”

The word makes Mydei jolt, his eyes no longer on his mouth but on his eyes. “You’ve been here a while and haven’t moved,” Mydei replies gruffly.

Phainon nods slowly, putting the water bottle down next to his laptop.

“Yeah, tough assignment. I still haven’t finished it.”

Mydei leans in, peering at the screen. “Sustainable and eco-friendly materials?”

Phainon sighs, “My favourite topic.” He says flatly.

“Come with me,” Mydei says suddenly and begins walking off before Phainon can reply. He sputters, scrambling up from his chair to chase after Mydei. It reminds him of the scene they made in the cafe, where now instead of coffee tables and patrons, it’s study tables and students they’re weaving around.

Phainon hasn’t been this far into the library before, getting lost amongst the identical shelves that tower above him. Mydei’s back is his only anchor, watching the way his hair sways with each step, his powerful legs striding confidently to wherever it is that they’re going. It’s now that Phainon realises that the tips of Mydei’s hair are reddish, almost strawberry blonde, curling at the ends cutely. Maybe the strawberry emoji he put next to his name wasn’t that bad of a choice, after all.

“This section should have what you need,” Mydei says as they come to a stop, and he turns to face the shelves. His fingers dance across the spines, tracing over the embossed lettering and plastic coverings as he picks one out and hands it over.

Phainon looks down, noting it’s one about sustainability in the eco-engineering world, and takes it, watching as Mydei selects another. It’s captivating watching him work like this, trailing through the books like he knows where every single one is off by heart. By the time Phainon has a stack of three clutched between his hands, weighing him down, Mydei looks rather pleased with himself.

“These should be enough,” Mydei says as he taps the top book’s cover, triumphant.

Phainon winces, barely managing to secure his grip before the precarious stack tilts dangerously close to one side. He scrambles to adjust, fingers slipping against the smooth covers, his breath catching as he fights to keep them tumbling straight to the floor.

Mydei sighs, a touch exasperated, but before Phainon can insist he’s got it, warm hands cup the backs of his, steadying them.

“Are they too heavy?” Mydei asks, voice quiet, closer.

Phainon’s joints lock up. It’s not the weight of the books that’s making his arms tense, his breath suddenly uneven - it’s the press of Mydei’s fingers against his own, the firm but careful way he guides his grip into something more secure. His touch is warm, grounding, and when their fingers begin to detangle, something sharp jolts through Phainon’s chest, catching him completely off guard.

He swears the entire library narrows down to this single point of contact, the warmth of Mydei’s skin against his own, the way their eyes lock, amber meeting blue in the dim lighting filtering through the shelves. The space between them feels tight, as though one sudden movement will snap it like an overwrought rubber band. Phainon can barely breathe, his chest constricting with the lack of oxygen, unable to move and look away, to break the spell he’s under. For a fleeting second, he sees it in Mydei’s eyes.

That softness, the way he’s been caught off guard by their touch, as though he feels something, too. But before he can pry that apart and delve deeper into it, Mydei pulls away.

Immediately, Phainon feels cold, a chill going all the way down to his bones. The absence of his touch is too abrupt, too confusing, sending him into overdrive.

“Be careful,” Mydei murmurs, his voice flat without a hint of concern, though there’s now a tension in his shoulders that wasn’t there before.

Phainon nods on autopilot. His hands feel clammy against the books as he curls his fingers tighter around them, determined to not let Mydei’s assistance go to waste.

“Thanks,” Phainon replies, just as quietly as how Mydei spoke.

Mydei nods back, and Phainon expects him to say something else - maybe a jab at how weak he is (which he isn’t, it’s just hard to fit going to the gym in between his studies), or give him more advice on books he can look at -

but Mydei does neither. He doesn’t linger like his touch and simply turns around, stepping away from the pocket of comfort they’d made for themselves, acting as though nothing happened.

Maybe it was nothing, but as Mydei walks away, leaving Phainon with his heart fluttering and warmth still radiating from where their hands touched, he can’t convince himself it's nothing at all.

Phainon is back at his dorm, essay finally submitted, and the stack of books he’d borrowed from the library piled high on his desk. They teeter dangerously on top of each other as if a sneeze would be enough to make them topple over. Phainon sighs, slumps in his desk chair, and pokes at the spine of the one in the middle. The pile doesn’t fall over, but it sways ominously. He hadn’t read much from any of them, but the bits found relevant to his essay did help. He should be happy that he’s done it again:

completed all his work for the week by the skin of his teeth, yet the victory doesn’t seem as sweet as knowing how Mydei’s hands feel on his.

The warmth still clings to his skin, phantom-like, refusing to fade. Phainon lifts his hands, turning them over in the low light as if searching for proof that Mydei had touched him there at all. His eyes trace the curve of his knuckles, the crescents of his cuticles, before flipping them over, palms up and fingers splayed.

Nothing.

No mark left behind, no evidence of that fleeting touch. Yet, as his forefinger drifts across the faint lines etched into his palm, he swears they feel different - like something unseen has settled beneath his skin, altering it in some quiet, irreversible way. The sensation hums there, just beyond the surface, stubborn and unseen no matter how hard he looks. Phainon swallows, finger coming to a stop at the love line on his palm, taking extra care to follow it from start to end. He taps over it, his fingers curling slightly when it tickles. He wonders idly how Mydei’s hands would feel elsewhere - maybe on his face, tangled in his hair or laced through his fingers, using the grip to pull them closer and closer until they’re chest to chest, breaths mingling.

With a start, Phainon snaps out of it. He slaps his cheeks between his palms, the sting welcomed as he wills his face to cool down. He’s glad that there’s no one here to see him blushing up to the roots of his hair. In a bout of shame, he glances towards the library books, his only witnesses. He swivels around on his chair, putting his back towards them as their spines glare holes into the back of his head. To give himself something to do, he picks up his phone lying at the foot of his bed and thumbs through his

notifications, stopping when he spots the text messaging app. He opens it up to his and Mydei’s conversation where his glaring mistake from earlier is still there, no less present than before.

It’s not that late, and considering the library shuts at midnight, surely Mydei will still be awake. It’s not even 11 pm yet. Phainon wants to text him so badly, but he’s not sure what to say. Mydei doesn’t seem the type to enjoy casual conversation or pointless small talk, but he has nothing else to go on.

They’re not close enough to ask soul-searching questions, or more personal ones about his background. He’s curious, desperately so, and wants to know everything about Mydei as quickly as he can consume it.

Baby steps, Phainon thinks and begins to type out a message.

[10:37 pm] Phainon:

thanks for the books, they rly helped

He doesn’t expect an immediate response, but that doesn’t stop him from checking his phone every few minutes, unable to help himself. It sits beside him on the desk, the screen dark and silent, yet it practically begs for his attention, beckoning him to take another look. Every time he glances at it, his pulse jumps slightly, anticipation curling low in his stomach, only to settle back into disappointment when there’s nothing new.

Minutes stretch into hours and nothing changes. He groans, finally giving up and tosses his phone back onto his bed so it’s out of reach, convinced that Mydei is either ignoring him (fair enough) or severely regretting ever

giving him his number (also fair enough). As he turns back to his laptop, he hears it, a ping signalling a text.

Phainon rockets out of his chair so fast that it wobbles dangerously, nearly toppling over in protest. He doesn’t care. Adrenaline propels him forward, and with all the grace of an overly excited puppy, he vaults over the back of it, landing on his bed with an unceremonious bounce. His knee smacks against the edge of the mattress, hitting the wooden bedframe, but the dull pain barely even registers as his eyes lock hungrily on his phone, screen glowing tantalisingly on the sheets.

He allows the momentum to carry him, lunging forward and grabbing at the device like a man starved, fingers fumbling in his desperation. The phone nearly slips out of his grasp, but he recovers quickly, trying to flatten his facial expression from eagerness to neutrality so his Face ID can recognise him. He clutches at it tightly, waiting patiently for the screen to unlock and open into his messages. His heart is hammering, his breath shallow, and in a startling moment of clarity, he realises that he probably looked like he was in the throes of some dramatic action movie sequence - except, instead of dodging bullets, he was just trying to read a text.

Still, as his eyes focus and confirm that Mydei has replied to him, the stakes feel just as high.

[12:01 am] Mydei :

That’s what they’re there for.

It’s short and sweet, simple and to the point, and so, so good. Phainon can almost hear Mydei saying it to his face, picturing the way he’d look as he said it: arms crossed, eyes narrowed behind his glasses, lips pressed in a straight line. Phainon groans out loud, head dipping forward in shame. He wants Mydei so badly that it’s making him go crazy, practically hallucinating voices and seeing things that aren’t there.

Determined to not let an opportunity go to waste, Phainon thinks, ideas bubbling and swirling in his brain until he finally hatches a plan. His plan isn’t one for the faint of heart or the less dedicated, but he’s neither of those things, so he’s convinced it’ll work. It has to.

Phainon’s plan unfolds slowly, just as he intended. It stretches across days, then weeks, eventually bleeding into springtime, settling into place as naturally as the lengthening days and the blooming of fresh flowers.

Without really thinking about it past surface level, he’s made Mydei a part of his daily routine - which, in turn, means that he must be a part of Mydei’s, too.

The first part of his plan is texting.

Every day, without fail, he sends Mydei a message. Sometimes it’s as simple as a good morning or good night, a quiet, persistent presence in his inbox. Other times, when he’s feeling braver, he’ll send a photo - blurry snapshots of his Word documents, the sun rising in streaks of pink and gold that secretly remind him of Mydei’s blushing face and eyes, a fleeting

moment captured during his walks to lectures, or even just a stupid cat meme he found online.

It’s the cat memes that get the most out of Mydei, breaking them out of his cycle of clipped replies and pulling something more from him - a full sentence, a wry comment, or, on the best days, a reaction. A thumbs-up emoji. A crying laughing face. A love heart. The latter sends Phainon’s own heart into a frantic tailspin, and he has to physically stop himself from over-analysing what it could mean. The heart isn’t meant for him, it’s meant for the cute fluffy kitten, which stupidly, he feels jealous of.

And the final part of his plan, inevitably, is the library visits. Those are more subtle and more carefully planned. Phainon tells himself repeatedly that it's not suspicious to turn up so often - he’s an engineering student, so of course, he needs to study and a quiet place to write essays - but he knows damn well that need has nothing to do with it. It’s simply all so he can catch a glimpse of Mydei, strike up more conversations with him in person, and borrow more books that he doesn’t even read, all so he can have more excuses to seek him out. The moments between them are brief, but they’re enough to keep Phainon coming back, over and over again, as his slow, careful plan continues to take root.

[11:17 am] Phainon:

hey mydei

are you at the library today?

[11:20 am] Mydei :

No. It’s my day off.

Phainon exhales heavily, staring down at his phone before pocketing it with a sigh that feels too dramatic, even for him. He scuffs his trainers against the pavement as he stalls, lingering outside the lecture hall as if standing here long enough might magically change the fact that Mydei isn’t at the library today.

He doesn’t know what to do with himself now. He’d already sat through his only class today, and he’d planned to spend the rest of it at the library - not that he’d admit to anyone that his studying was secondary to simply being near Mydei. Even from a distance, just existing in the same place as him had become part of his routine, a quiet comfort he hadn’t realised he relied on until now. It was a fair trade: he got to see his crush and be productive at the same time. It was a win-win. This? This is a lose-lose; no Mydei, no studying.

This throws a wrench in everything. He’d been lucky the past few weeks, his schedule aligning perfectly with Mydei’s shifts, but he supposed that streak had to end at some point. Still, he’s surprised by the pang of disappointment settling in his chest, heavier than it should be considering he can easily see him another time. Shaking it off the best he can, he runs through his options: he could go back to his dorm, or maybe hang out in the common area and see if there’s any new campus gossip floating around.

Neither seems to hold much appeal to him, stuck between spending time on his own or around people who aren’t Mydei.

Then, another idea pops into his head. The cafe.

A warm drink, something sweet to eat alongside it - yeah, that sounds better than moping around. Maybe it’ll even lift his mood a little, and that’ll be even better. Without giving himself time to overthink it past that, he adjusts the strap of his bag over his shoulder and heads off towards it.

As the bell above the door jingles, Phainon steps inside, immediately enveloped by the warm, familiar scent of coffee and cinnamon. The rich aroma is comforting enough to ease the disappointment still lingering in his chest, and he’s very glad he decided to come here.

The cafe is bustling, every table occupied with students hunched over laptops, friends chatting over half-finished pastries and the occasional solitary person scrolling on their phone. Phainon rocks onto his tiptoes, scanning the back of the room in search of an open seat. He doesn’t mind sitting by strangers, per se, but he’d much rather have a spot of his own. But instead of finding an empty table, his gaze lands on something - or rather, someone - much more appealing.

Blonde hair catches the soft glow of the cafe lights, a pair of black-framed glasses perched on a familiar nose, a book held effortlessly in one hand.

Phainon’s breath hitches, pulse thundering in his ears. Mydei. He barely hesitates. The moment he spots the librarian tucked into the corner of the cafe, he’s moving - forgetting all about his own order. His feet carry him forward before his mind fully catches up, following the magnetic pull tugging at him to come closer.

chapters.html:
Mydei is exactly how Phainon always pictured him: alone, absorbed in a book, fingers gently holding the spine with a delicacy that comes from attentiveness. His other hand cradles a mug, steam curling lazily into the air.

He looks comfortable, settled into the worn leather of the sofa like he’s been there for hours. Maybe he has, and Phainon’s about to ruin his solitude by interrupting him. He hates how badly he wants to be a part of it - to sit beside him, to disrupt whatever peace Mydei has wrapped himself in just so he can be included within.

Phainon doesn’t think, doesn’t second-guess himself. He stops in front of Mydei’s seat, waiting patiently to be noticed by a pair of amber eyes that eventually drag themselves away from the pages of his book. For a moment, there’s no recognition, just mild surprise at being disturbed, until it turns into something else, softening the corners of Mydei’s sharp eyes and sharper lips.

“So this is what you do on your days off?” Phainon says, eager to talk with the other man.

“Are you following me?” Mydei asks instead of answering.

Phainon laughs, “Please, you wish I was that obsessed with you.”

Except, to his dawning realisation, he is that obsessed with Mydei.

Thankfully, Mydei doesn’t deign him with a response to that, opting to raise an eyebrow and let out a noncommittal hum.

Mydei jerks his chin upwards, “No hot chocolate today?”

Phainon shrugs, “Haven’t made up my mind on what I wanna order yet.” A minor lie, but one he can’t get called out on. He leans over to peer into Mydei’s mug, taking in the bright red liquid. “Pomegranate milk again?”

“Yes, but I asked them to warm it up this time,” Mydei extends his arm, offering it to him. “Try it.”

Phainon hesitates for only a second, blinking a few times in shock, before wrapping his fingers around the handle to bring it towards him. His eyes flicker up to meet Mydei’s, searching, testing. Slowly, making sure that Mydei’s eyes are still on him and only him, he deliberately twists the mug in his grasp, aligning his lips with the exact spot that Mydei’s had just been.

His gaze never wavers as he takes a sip, the warm liquid coating his tongue.

It’s a lot nicer than he expected it to be. It’s sweet, but not overwhelmingly so, and he hums in quiet approval before giving the mug back. His fingers purposely brush against Mydei’s as he does, the simple touch sending a shiver down his spine.

Mydei doesn’t look away either. He accepts the mug with the same steady ease as it was offered to him, tilting it towards his lips. Phainon watches, entranced, as Mydei takes another sip - from the exact same place that Phainon just had. Phainon’s heart jackrabbits in his chest, the pit of his stomach swirling dangerously. He grits his teeth as Mydei places the mug back down on the table, watching as he swipes his tongue across his bottom lip to catch a stray drop of milk. It makes his lips look even pinker than before, the pomegranate syrup staining them slightly. Phainon wants to reach out and grab him by the chin, tilting his head back just enough that he can sweep in and kiss him, licking the taste of the fruity milk right out of

his mouth. He wonders how much nicer it’ll taste then, how much sweeter it’d be, how -

“Good?” Mydei’s voice interrupts his thoughts.

“Yeah,” Phainon replies, suspiciously breathy. He clears his throat, “Very sweet, just like you.” He throws on at the end, sending Mydei a blinding smile along with it.

Mydei grimaces, completely unphased. “Flirt.”

“Only just noticed?” Phainon replies, strangely emboldened after their indirect kiss.

Mydei’s eyes glow with mirth, lips tugging up ever so slightly in the corners. Phainon wants to consume him.

“You’re not exactly subtle.”

“Is that why you gave me your number?” Phainon asks, genuinely curious.

“No,” Mydei replies and doesn’t elaborate. He gestures towards the front counter instead, “Go and order before you get kicked out for loitering.”

“Can I come back and sit with you?”

“Do whatever you want.”

“But,” Phainon begins, taking a step closer, hip nudging the side of the table as he crowds into Mydei’s space, their knees knocking together. Mydei looks shocked, lips parted and eyes wide as he looks up at Phainon. It’s a great expression on him, one that Phainon wants to savour, to hide from the rest of the world so only he can see it. “What do you want?”

“Doesn’t matter,” Mydei replies, voice hoarse.

“It does,” Phainon rephrases: “It matters to me what you want.”

Mydei breathes out, pupils blown as he blinks up at Phainon. He speaks slowly: “I want you to go and get your damn drink and stop pestering me.”

“I can do that,” Phainon grins, “I’ll be back in a bit.”

Mydei waves him off dismissively, immediately going back to his book.

Phainon feels like he’s on cloud nine as he waltzes over to the front counter to put in his order. He doesn’t ask for pomegranate milk as much as he wants to, opting for a simple latte instead. He takes it back to the table, smiling brightly when he sees that Mydei has put his book away. That means that he intends to talk, right? Not just read his book and ignore him for the entire time, which is what Phainon expected would happen.

Progress, progress, Phainon thinks happily to himself, humming a happy tune as he sits down next to Mydei, their shoulders and thighs touching. He folds one leg over the other, almost giddy with how pleased he is.

“I changed my mind, go sit somewhere else.”

“Oh, c’mon, don’t be a spoilsport,” Phainon chimes, knocking their shoulders together playfully. It gets him the reaction he wants: a scowl and piercing eyes glaring at him.

Phainon takes a cautious sip of his drink to hide his grin, only to realise too late that it’s still too hot. A shocked gasp escapes him as he quickly sticks his tongue out, hoping the cool air will soothe the burn.

“You look like a dog when you do that,” Mydei remarks snidely.

“So mean,” Phainon whines, wincing when his tongue throbs from the burn.

“A latte?” Mydei questions, ignoring Phainon’s insult.

“I usually order this, you just caught me on a bad day when I got the hot chocolate,” Phainon laughs.

Mydei leans into the arm of the chair, away from Phainon, propping his elbow up on it and resting his cheek in the palm of his hand, eyes darting back to him. “Not quite a triple-shot espresso, but it’s an improvement.”

Phainon grumbles, “I still don’t get what you have against hot chocolate when you’re drinking pomegranate milk.”

Mydei shrugs, “My mother used to make it for me as a kid, and it just stuck.”

“Oh,” Phainon blinks, a bit taken aback by the sudden personal anecdote.

He wasn’t expecting that without purposely prying, so he added this small tidbit into the back of his mind for later. “I’m sure she’s glad you still drink it.”

Mydei’s lips curl into a smile, but there’s no real warmth behind it. It’s the kind of smile that doesn’t quite reach his eyes, one that wavers at the edges as though it’ll crumble at any moment. His gaze is distant, unfocused as if he’s looking past Phainon, past the cafe, past the very moment they’re in.

“She would’ve been happy, yes,” Mydei says, voice hollow.

His fingers tighten ever so slightly around the handle of his mug, knuckles paling from the pressure. For a fleeting second, Phainon sees it - the weight of something unspoken pressing down on him, an open wound that still hasn’t fully healed. Phainon wants to say something, to bridge the space between them and gently bring Mydei back to the present, but the words catch in his throat. What can he say? Instead, he watches, giving Mydei a private moment to himself.

Within the next few seconds, his faraway expression is gone, replaced with one that’s far more familiar to Phainon.

To try and lift the mood, Phainon asks: “What were you reading before I came in?”

Mydei blinks before leaning forward and grabbing the book from his bag on the floor. “Mortal and Divine, it’s a collection of Greek poetry.”

Phainon takes the book from Mydei’s hands. It’s a worn copy, clear by how the pages are slightly yellowed on the edges, but apart from that, there are no signs of wear and tear. He inspects it, noting the spine is still pristine, not a crease in sight. He flicks through a few pages, being careful not to open it fully and damage it. His eyes trail over the words, them mostly going over his head. Poetry in general isn’t his idea of fun reading, but each poem has a small illustration above it which draws his interest. He lingers on a few that catch his eye until he flips to a full page one. Phainon turns the book horizontally to get a better look at it. An inked illustration shows a lone

figure standing at the entrance of a towering marble temple, their raised arms bathed in blood as they hold up a sword. Faceless gods loom above them in the sky, watching the figure, partially hidden behind clouds.

“Some pretty hard-hitting stuff,” Phainon remarks, closing the book gently and handing it back to Mydei. “Is that from the library?”

“No, it’s from my personal collection,” Mydei takes the book back, the very tips of their fingers touching. It sends an electric shock through Phainon. “It was a gift from my mother.”

Another mention of his mother. The words settle heavily between them, and Phainon feels an almost unbearable pull - a desperate need to reach out, to comfort and to know. Every piece of Mydei that he’s been given so far has just been that: a piece. A mere fragment of something much larger, something he hasn’t yet been allowed to see in full.

Phainon wants to ask. The urge claws at his chest, twisting so tight around his lungs that he feels breathless. He wants to know what Mydei’s mother was like, if she was anything like him. He wants to press, to peel back the guarded layers Mydei keeps so firmly in place and see him, truly, fully.

But he doesn’t. Because he knows what it’s like to have something sacred and personal pried from his grip when he’s not ready to let it go. He knows the sting of questions asked too soon, the way they can turn a tender memory into something sharp and painful, and the last thing Phainon wants is to be the reason Mydei retreats even more into himself, especially when they’ve come this far already.

So instead, he swallows down his curiosity, his yearning to reach out and tangle their fingers together to squeeze them encouragingly, and lets the moment pass by.

“You’ve taken care of it very well.”

Mydei nods in affirmation, clearly proud of himself. “It’s what inspired me to become a librarian.”

“Oh?” Phainon leans into Mydei, pressing their shoulders together firmly, latte forgotten as he watches the other with a newfound interest. “And not because you wanted to help poor, stressed-out students like me pass their exams?” Phainon jokes, batting his eyelashes dramatically with his words.

Mydei rolls his eyes, turning at the waist to face Phainon. He lands a solid flick to the middle of Phainon’s forehead. It hurts, the bastard, and he pouts while he rubs at the sore spot as Mydei settles back down.

“You’re so cruel!”

“You haven’t even seen the half of it, Phainon,” Mydei replies, tone snide.

Phainon freezes. The world around him dulls, fading into a distant hum as all his focus zeroes in on one thing: his name, spoken by Mydei. His hand falls limply into his lap, fingers slack against the fabric of his jeans, discarded. It takes him a moment to process, to fully grasp the weight of it, but once he does, it settles into his chest like a slow-burning ember.

Phainon has heard his name countless times before: casual greetings from classmates, impatient scoldings from his parents and professors, teasing remarks from Castorice. But this - this is different. It isn’t just the sound of it, but the way it lingers, warm and careful, shaped by Mydei’s deep voice and delicate lips. His throat tightens, pulse thrumming against his skin, too fast, too much.

“I think that’s the first time you’ve ever said my name,” Phainon croaks out.

Mydei’s expression scrunches up, adjusting the glasses on his face to sit higher on his nose bridge. “I’ve said your name before.”
